cohort: The study enrolled 30 pregnant individuals at >=28 weeks of gestation, consisting of 16 with preeclampsia and 14 normotensive controls, excluding those with chronic hypertension, neurologic or developmental disabilities, moderate or severe depression or anxiety, or current substance use.
finding: People with preeclampsia reported worse subjective memory and scored lower in attention, working memory, and executive function compared with normotensive people, even after adjusting for time, age, education, and prepregnancy body mass index.
